caption.text:
There are seasons in life where simply continuing is an act of courage. Days where getting out of bed, answering messages, showing up to work, or just breathing through the heaviness feels like more than anyone around you realizes. Grief does not only live in the moments we lose someone — it lives in the quiet spaces afterward, in the ways life continues when your heart still feels paused. 

So if you are carrying something heavy right now — a loss, a heartbreak, a disappointment, a chapter you never expected to live through — please know that surviving it is already something to be proud of. You may feel like you are barely holding it together, but even that is a form of strength. Healing does not always look graceful. Sometimes it just looks like making it through the day. 

Grief asks you to walk through things you never should have had to face. And yet here you are, still moving forward in whatever way you can. That deserves gentleness. That deserves compassion. That deserves recognition. 

— Words from the book ‘If You’re Grieving’ by Jacqueline Whitney 🖤📖 @jacquelinewhitney_

latest_comments: Trying to heal while still having to show up in other areas of your life as if nothing’s wrong is such a struggle. It feels like you’re being pulled in four different directions at the same time. You get overwhelmed by your emotions, but you have to act like you’re doing fine so no one notices that you’re slowly dying inside.
I needed these words. Thank you 🤍
